metas.name: Bollard - Black Rectangle
metas.note:
Flat bollards, or cylindrical bollards with a black rectangle containing the reflector are most commonly found on major roads in the northern half of the country.

Beware that one type of flat bollards can look similar to the cyllindrical bollards, however the black section here is not horizontal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Bollard - Skåne
metas.note:
These small white bollards with either a blue or a red strip near the top can be found in the countryside of Skåne.

NOTE: You may occasionally find similar bollards in urban areas further north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Bollard - Wedge Shaped
metas.note: Wedge-shaped bollards, similar to those found in Germany, are most common in the southern regions of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Cylindrical Bollards
metas.note: Cylindrical bollards, with a completely horizontal black section near the top, are most commonly found near the west coast and in Värmland and southern Dalarna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Dalarna Wooden Craftmanship
metas.note:
Central Dalarna has a strong tradition of wooden craftsmanship, and as a result much of the architecture has a unique, picturesque look to it. Most commonly, you may find red timbered houses, portals made of logs, and so-called härbren which have a very distinct design.

NOTE: Similar buildings can be found elsewhere in the country, but it is by far most common in central Dalarna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Gotland Limestone Houses
metas.note: Houses on Gotland are commonly made of limestone and often have a dirty-looking white facade. Churches on Gotland are very distinct looking, with either grey walls or white walls with grey corners, a large portal around the door and small windows typically divided in two by a pillar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Gotland White Sand
metas.note: White sand can often be seen next to roads on Gotland. It is typically more noticeable in the northern half of the island and on Fårö.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Hälsingland Houses
metas.note: Hälsingland has many big, mostly red, farmhouses. They are characterised by many large windows, 2–3 floors, and the front facade being long and grand-looking. Barns can also be seen having an unusual amount of windows in the region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Mälaren Fields
metas.note: The area surrounding lake Mälaren can often be recognized by the fairly flat ground with medium sized agricultural fields, forests beyond them, and small “islands” of bushes and trees in the middle of the fields.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Max South Beech Forests
metas.note: Beech forests, which can generally be recognised by the barren ground covered in brown leafs, are mainly found in the far south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: North Coast Shed Roofs
metas.note: Along the northern coast you will commonly encounter agricultural sheds which are either octagonal or rectangular, with the walls noticeably leaning outwards. They will typically be made out of red-painted logs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Northern Birch Rows
metas.note: It is very common to see long, neat rows of moderately thin birches in urban areas along the north coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Northern Boreal Trees
metas.note: This type of vegetation, consisting of thin, weak-looking boreal trees and somewhat sandy soil can be found in the far north of Sweden.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Northern Fields
metas.note: If you see flat, medium-sized to small agricultural fields, and you suspect that you are in the northern half of the country, you are likely somewhat close to the coast between Umeå and Luleå.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Northern Jämtland Dirt Roads
metas.note: Dirt roads which have a deep grey colour and are aligned with low, green grassy vegetation on either side are commonly found in the northern half of Jämtland. This is mostly found in Generation 4 summer and Generation 3 fall coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Northern Sheet Metal Roofs
metas.note: Grey metal roofs on residential buildings generally get more common the further north in the country you get. Note that metal roofs on barns and sheds can be found significantly further south.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Öland Low Rock Walls
metas.note: Öland is an extremely flat island with a somewhat barren south half with many small bushes, while the north is typically slightly lusher with fewer, but larger bushes and some trees. The island also contains a very large number of small rock walls.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Öland/Gotland Uneven Stone Brick
metas.note: This type of uneven stone brick is typically found in houses and rock walls on Öland, and less commonly in rock walls on Gotland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Red Dirt
metas.note: Red dirt roads are mainly found in Dalarna, but can also be found in and around Kalmar county, the border between inland Norrbotten and Västerbotten, and rarely between lakes Vänern and Vättern.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Red Roads
metas.note:
Many roads in western Dalarna and nearby regions have a very noticeable red colour.

NOTE: Forests in the region predominantly consist of thin pines, which, in combination with the red roads, is a very good indication of the region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Skåne Fields
metas.note: In Skåne you will find the most open agricultural landscape in Sweden. It is the only region where, rather than a dense forest in the distance, you can get only a few small patches of trees strewn across the fields. On top of that, crops are often more diverse than the cereal crops, which are typical for the rest of Sweden.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Skåne Houses -  Half Timbered
metas.note: Half-timbered houses can be found mainly in the southern half of Skåne, but also in the northern half and southern Halland. It can also be found in Visby on rare occasions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Skåne Houses - Coloured Wooden Triangle
metas.note: Houses in Skåne commonly have either a white stone, or a red brick wall with a coloured wooden triangle beneath the roof on the sides. Similar houses with other materials (such as grey brick) for the walls can be found elsewhere in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Skåne Houses - Red Brick
metas.note: A lot of single family houses in Skåne are built out of red brick. They typically look slightly older than red brick houses in other parts of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Snowmobile Trail Red Cross
metas.note: Small red crosses marking snowmobile trails can be found throughout the northern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Södermanland Fields
metas.note: Agricultural fields in and around Södermanland very often go through small valleys, with forests up on the sides of the valleys. The fields are typically medium to small sized.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Southern Broadleaf Tree
metas.note: Broad leafed trees, other than birches, only grow naturally in the southern half of the country, and become increasingly common the further south you get. · Images and descriptions courtesy of Plonkit.net Check out plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Southern Corrugated Square Metal Roofs
metas.note: Corrugated square metal roof panels with moss growing on them are typically found in southern Sweden, particularly in Skåne and Blekinge. It is mainly found on large barns, and the roofs are often very steep.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Southern Diamond Tiled Roofs
metas.note:
Grey diamond-tiled roofs are mainly found in Skåne, Blekinge, Öland, and occasionally on Gotland.

NOTE: Gotland and Öland are normally more easily recognised from landscape alone. Houses in western and southern Skåne typically use a lot of stone and bricks, while houses in northeastern Skåne and Blekinge are mostly made of red painted wood.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Southern Ferns
metas.note: Ferns are mostly found in southern and central Sweden. They can occasionally be found further north in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Southern Rock Walls
metas.note:
Rock walls are mainly found in the south, with the largest concentration being in several coastal areas, on Öland, and on the southern and northern tips of Gotland.

Beware that rock walls around churches and cemeteries are common further north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Storsjön Fields
metas.note: In most of Jämtland County, particularly around lake Storsjön, you can find large farmlands, commonly situated in the middle of wide, often somewhat steep hills, which is uncommon in the rest of the country, where most farmlands will be either on flat ground or in valleys. The fields are generally not cultivated and will mostly consist of ordinary grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Tree-less Mountains
metas.note: While it is possible to see forested mountains in several regions in the country, mountains with no trees at the top can only be found in the northwestern parts of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Umeå Snow Pole
metas.note: Green snow poles can occasionally be found in the area surrounding Umeå.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Västergötland / Östergötland Fields
metas.note: The agricultural landscape of Västergötland and Östergötland is mostly flat, similarly to the landscape around lake Mälaren. The two most consistent differences is that this landscape is more open and has lots of wind turbines. While you can almost always see a forest in the distance, it will typically be much further away than around Mälaren.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Västernorrland Hills
metas.note: The landscape around the High Coast in Västernorrland can be recognised by the many forested, rocky mountains surrounding agricultural valleys. The valleys are rarely straight and the mountains are of varying heights and shapes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: West Coast Exposed Rocks
metas.note:
It is very common to see exposed, often somewhat round, rocks on the Swedish west coast. They will often have lower vegetation, such as small bushes, growing on them.

NOTE: Exposed rocks around Stockholm are also fairly common, however these typically look sharper than rocks on the west coast, and commonly have thick moss growing on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: West Coast Fields
metas.note: On the west coast, and particularly in Halland, you will see a lot of flat agricultural fields with small, round, forested hills in the distance. Generally, the hills get larger and the fields get smaller further north. The area also has more precipitation than most of the country, and as such it typically looks very lush.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: West Coast Red Shed Rows
metas.note: Dense rows of very small red sheds are commonly found in coastal towns on the northern west coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: West Coast White Houses
metas.note: While houses in Sweden are mostly very colourful, on the west coast they are commonly much lighter. There are an especially large number of white and light yellow houses along the coast between Gothenburg and the Norwegian border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.
